boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Loras spaces whose everyday academic, community, recreational, or reflective uses are documented by current college and library sources.

cards.entity_name: Bill and JoAnne Miller Academic Resource Center
cards.title: Build a Study Plan Around the MARC
cards.subtitle: Library resources, media tools, tutoring, and varied study seating
cards.notes: Start at the main-floor service desk, then choose an individual or group study area that fits the assignment you brought.
cards.short_summary: The MARC combines library collections, academic support, media equipment, and multiple study-space formats in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras states that the MARC houses its library, Learning Commons, media studios, disability resources, career guidance, and study spaces.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Campus access and individual services may follow college or library schedules; consult the library’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Bring the Stuck Part to the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: A specific place for tutoring, writing help, math questions, and study skills
cards.notes: Arrive with a draft, problem set, or time-management question so staff can focus the session on a concrete next step.
cards.short_summary: This MARC-based academic support space connects students with targeted help rather than requiring them to navigate separate offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras describes the Learning Commons as a collaboration of campus resources supporting tutoring, academic coaching, writing, math, and study skills.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources | Student Success | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Services are intended for Loras students; appointment, drop-in, and operating arrangements can vary by program.

cards.title: Use the ACC as a Campus Errand Hub
cards.subtitle: Student services, food, mail, technology help, and involvement offices
cards.notes: Bundle practical stops here: check mail, ask Student Life a question, visit the IT desk, or find the office tied to your next task.
cards.short_summary: The ACC is useful as a multi-stop service building, with several daily student needs gathered under one roof.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras says the Alumni Campus Center contains the post office, health and counseling services, IT help desk, dining, Campus Life, Spiritual Life, Campus Safety, and inclusion offices.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Individual offices and dining operations maintain separate schedules and may restrict some services to students.

cards.title: Pair a South-Campus Break With the Lounge
cards.subtitle: A named café and meet-up space on the south side of campus
cards.notes: Use the lounge for a short meet-up or study interval, and check current dining details before counting on food service.
cards.short_summary: Loras explicitly presents the Einstein Bros. lounge as a place where students can meet or study between other campus commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: The college dining page identifies Einstein Bros. Bagels on the south side of campus and specifically invites students to meet, study, and use its lounge area.
cards.source_title: Dining on Campus, Food Options & Meal Plans | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; seating availability and operating hours follow the campus dining schedule.

cards.title: Find the Chapel’s Participatory Side
cards.subtitle: Worship, music ministry, faith-sharing, and community groups
cards.notes: Check Spiritual Life’s schedule, then attend an appropriate service or ask how to join music, hospitality, or faith-sharing activities.
cards.short_summary: The chapel supports both quiet religious use and organized forms of student participation through Spiritual Life.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras documents Christ the King Chapel as a place for worship, music ministry, daily Mass, faith-sharing groups, and student or community groups.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Religious services and group activities follow published schedules; enter respectfully when the chapel is available.

cards.title: Look Beyond Game Day at Lillis AWC
cards.subtitle: Campus fitness facilities alongside varsity athletics spaces
cards.notes: Check current recreation access before arriving, then use the fitness facilities or attend an eligible campus athletics activity.
cards.short_summary: The center serves everyday campus fitness as well as housing several varsity programs and athletics support functions.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras identifies the Lillis AWC as the home of campus fitness facilities, athletic training, locker rooms, athletics offices, and several varsity teams.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Fitness and athletics areas may require college identification, team authorization, or adherence to scheduled facility access.

cards.title: See What Students Put on the Dome
cards.subtitle: Student-presented monthly astronomy shows for campus and community audiences
cards.notes: Choose a listed public show and reserve or purchase admission through the official page rather than assuming walk-in space.
cards.short_summary: The planetarium gives students from different majors a public-facing venue for presenting astronomy topics.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras says the Heitkamp Memorial Planetarium hosts monthly shows presented by students in different majors and open to students and the Dubuque community.
cards.access_notes: Attend only a currently listed public show or confirmed private booking; the venue has no water fountain or bathrooms.

cards.title: Wait for a Scheduled Observatory Opening
cards.subtitle: A campus telescope space used for student stargazing
cards.notes: Watch for an announced opening and dress for outdoor conditions; do not treat the observatory as an always-open drop-in space.
cards.short_summary: The observatory offers a scheduled, hands-on complement to the nearby planetarium’s indoor presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras states that students can conduct their own star-searching in the campus observatory when it is open at scheduled times.
cards.access_notes: Access is limited to scheduled opening times; verify an announced session before going to the observatory.

cards.entity_name: Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes
cards.title: Pause at the Campus Grotto
cards.subtitle: A named Marian shrine in the middle of campus since 1954
cards.notes: Use the grotto for a quiet pause or documented campus observance, keeping conversation and photography respectful of worshippers.
cards.short_summary: This centrally located outdoor shrine adds a reflective space with a documented connection to Loras’s mid-century campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras College Digital Collections documents that the Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes opened in the middle of campus in 1954.
cards.source_title: Religion · Life at Loras: A Retrospective of 1950's Campus Life
cards.access_notes: The grotto is an outdoor religious site; respect ceremonies, private prayer, campus rules, and any temporary restrictions.

cards.title: Use the MARC Lawn as a Group Rendezvous
cards.subtitle: An officially named outdoor gathering point beside the academic resource center
cards.notes: Name the lawn as the meeting point, bring weather-appropriate seating, and move indoors if a college program has reserved the area.
cards.short_summary: The lawn works as an easy-to-describe outdoor assembly point next to one of the campus’s main academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras’s official student orientation schedule names MARC Lawn as the location for an interactive student group session called Meet Your Flock.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent and may be displaced by scheduled college programming or campus access restrictions.
